title: Dynamic Log Aggregator Scaling
business: A cloud-native logging service that processes high-velocity telemetry streams from distributed microservices.
problem: The system uses a dynamic array to buffer incoming log entries. When the buffer reaches capacity, it must allocate a new, larger array and copy all existing entries, causing occasional high-latency spikes that degrade real-time monitoring.
solution: Amortized analysis demonstrates that while a single resize operation is expensive, the average cost per insertion remains constant over a sequence of operations. By doubling the array size during each resize, the total cost of all resizes is spread across enough insertions to maintain a low, predictable average cost.
steps: Initialize a dynamic array with a fixed starting capacity.
Perform insertions by adding elements to the next available index.
Trigger a resize operation only when the current capacity is exhausted.
Allocate a new array with double the current capacity and copy all existing elements.
Deallocate the old array and resume standard insertions.
outcome: The system achieves consistent throughput for log ingestion, as the infrequent, high-cost resize operations are effectively neutralized by the high volume of low-cost insertions.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is memory overhead, as the array may remain partially empty after a resize. To check this, monitor the load factor, defined as the ratio of occupied slots to total capacity, to ensure it does not drop below a predefined threshold.

questions.question: In Dynamic Log Aggregator Scaling, why does the system experience occasional latency spikes?
options: Because the system must allocate a new array and copy existing entries when the buffer is full.
Because the system processes telemetry streams from too many microservices simultaneously.
Because the average cost of insertion is too high for real-time monitoring.
Because the load factor of the dynamic array is kept too low.
questions.explanation: The problem description explicitly identifies the resize and copy process as the cause of the latency spikes.
questions.evidence: When the buffer reaches capacity, it must allocate a new, larger array and copy all existing entries, causing occasional high-latency spikes that degrade real-time monitoring.

questions.question: In Dynamic Log Aggregator Scaling, what is the primary tradeoff of using this amortized approach?
options: Increased CPU usage during every single insertion operation.
The risk of the system becoming non-deterministic due to probability.
Memory overhead resulting from partially empty arrays after resizing.
The inability to handle high-velocity telemetry streams.
questions.explanation: The limitation section highlights memory overhead as the tradeoff for the amortized performance gains.
questions.evidence: The primary tradeoff is memory overhead, as the array may remain partially empty after a resize.
